gaps.sentence: The team played ___ and deserved to win (EXCELLENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'played': excellently (-ly).

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INVENT) of the new engine worked day and night.
gaps.explanation: The person who worked day and night is the inventor; 'invention' is the thing created.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather is still very ___ for his age (ACT).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'very': active (-ive). 'Activity' is a noun and 'actively' an adverb.

gaps.sentence: The referee sent him off for repeated ___ (OBEY).
gaps.explanation: 'Repeated disobedience' — the negative noun follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: We had no ___ (CHOOSE) but to cancel the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Have no choice but to do something' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'choose' is an irregular 'choice'.

gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The instructions were unclear, so I had to ___ them completely (WRITE).
gaps.hint: write again — unclear the first time (re-); base verb needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rewrite. A base verb is needed after 'had to'.
